intro: The monitoring network of WP4 is chosen by one objective function that joins three results. It is goal-oriented: a sensor is valued by the expected information it gives about the decision quantity, the salt mass near the toe of the wedge or whether a supply well exceeds its limit, through the adjoint sensitivities of the coupled model. It is robust: the information is taken in the worst case over the error parameters that are known only within a box, the max–min design of Chowdhary, Attia and Alexanderian {ref:roed}. It is free of interference and certified: the errors that sensors share through their data-logger hubs are corrected by sealed reference channels chosen beside the piezometers (INTERVENTION-GO, the proposal of the author's state of the art on interfering sensors), and every chosen network carries an upper bound on what any network of the same size could achieve, from the noise-inflation relaxation and the Frank–Wolfe certificate of the author's Certified OED framework (Zeqiraj, working draft, October 2026; Theorems 8 and 15). The computation below is the MATLAB script robust_certified_network.m, which uses the functions of the package unchanged and was run in GNU Octave 8.4 on the test section of the package (12 candidate salinity sensors on four hubs, sensor noise 2% of sea-water salinity).

equations.what: The noise of the 12 candidates: independent sensor noise, a common error per data-logger hub and a model error correlated over a length $\ell$; $\theta=(a,\ell)$ is known only within a box:

The objective function: the worst-case goal-oriented information of the piezometers $S$ and the reference channels $R$ (rows of zero sensitivity whose noise is the hub error), maximised over the designs within the budget:

The certificate, computed without enumerating the designs: for any relaxed point $\bar w$ of the capped simplex, any scenarios $\theta_j$ in the box and any weights $\lambda_j$, the noise-inflation relaxation $r^2_j$ (exact at binary designs and concave) and its Frank–Wolfe gap bound the robust optimum from above:
tex: \bar U_k=\min\left\{\max_{R_0}\left[\sum_j\lambda_j r^2_{j,R_0}(\bar w)+\gamma_{\mathrm{FW}}\left(\sum_j\lambda_j\nabla r^2_{j,R_0}(\bar w),\,\bar w\right)\right],\ U_{\mathrm{ceil}},\ U_{\mathrm{full}}\right\}

results: The worst hub-error amplitude is always the upper end of its range (2200 of 2200 pairs of design and goal), while the worst correlation length depends on the design and lies inside its range for 42% of the pairs, as robust design theory predicts. The network chosen when the interference is ignored, sensors [4, 7, 8], claims 2.539 nats about the salt mass near the toe but guarantees only 1.682 nats (−34%). The robust exhaustive optimum [4, 7, 9] guarantees 1.782 nats (+6%), and adding one sealed reference channel on hub 3 gives the robust optimum [4, 6, 7] + r3 with 1.970 nats (+17%); both robust networks spend one low-signal sensor at the top of a hub to read that hub's common error, a choice that no independent-noise criterion can make. For the question "is the supply cell above its limit?", the network that ignores the interference, [7, 8, 11], claims 0.592 nats and guarantees 0.519, against 0.530 for the robust network [7, 9, 11] and 0.545 for [7, 10, 11] + r3. The certificate bounds the robust optimum at 1.988 nats (salt mass) and 0.548 nats (supply question), so the chosen networks are certified within 0.9% and 0.5% of the best possible network; over 3–6 sensors, with or without a reference channel, every certified gap is at most 2.3%, and robust greedy selection with exchange found the exhaustive robust optimum in all 16 cases tested.

All information values were confirmed by direct Gaussian conditioning on the hub errors (differences below 2·10⁻¹⁴ nats) and by Monte Carlo simulation (within one standard error), and without interference the method returns the designs [4, 7, 8] (2.539 nats) and [7, 8, 11] of the package example. The yes/no information is integrated accurately here; the 24-node Gauss–Hermite rule of version 0.1.0 underestimates it when the data explain more than about 90% of the variance, without changing the ranking of the designs, and the accurate rule used here, a change of variable before the quadrature, can replace it in the next version of the code.

scheme_text: **How the certified design differs from the standard pipeline.** Optimal sensor placement for Bayesian inverse problems governed by partial differential equations is usually carried out as in the review of Alexanderian {ref:alex21}. Figure {fig} compares that pipeline, step by step, with the Certified OED framework on which this objective function rests; C1–C10 mark where a contribution of the framework enters and which step of the review it analyses or corrects. Every criterion, gradient, Hessian and greedy step is computed exactly in data space after a one-time cost of $n_s$ adjoint (and $n_s$ forward) solves, where the review uses trace estimators or subspace iteration in every iteration of the optimiser (C1, C7). The relaxation is characterised exactly: it is strictly convex if and only if the rank-one terms are independent, which fails for the c-criterion, whereas the review states that the c-criterion is strictly convex for a full-rank forward map (C2, C3). Greedy selection carries guarantees, since the expected information gain is submodular and the A-criterion weakly submodular with ratio $\gamma\ge 1/(1+\mathrm{SNR}_{\max})$ (C4), and correlated noise is treated by a parallel-sum relaxation that is exact at binary designs, where naive weighting overstates the information (C5). Above all, every design leaves with a certificate: for linear designs a certified optimality gap from the Frank–Wolfe duality gap and from interlacing, Hadamard and Weyl bounds, with design values that are independent of the mesh (C3, C6); for nonlinear designs two-sided information bounds from one sample of forward runs reused for every subset (C8); and, for a decision quantity, bounds on its expected posterior variance (C9, C10). The review returns a design without an optimality certificate. This section adds to the framework the worst case over the error parameters and the reference channels.
